text:

o Your model should include countries that have yet to earn medals; what is your projection for how many will earn their first medal in the next Olympics? What sort of odds do you give to this estimate? o Your model should also consider the events (number and types) at a given Olympics. title: Hack-a-thon
text:
Data Cleaning

I dropped the ID columns since they were not needed.
I added a year obligation over annual income to see how much money per year was already going to previous obligations.
I added a late payment over num credit lines to see if people who added lots of credit lines also paid late.



Code
X_train['year_debt_to_income_no_loan'] = X_train['monthly_obligations'] * 12 / X_train['annual_income']
X_test['year_debt_to_income_no_loan'] = X_test['monthly_obligations'] * 12 / X_test['annual_income']

X_train['late_payments_per_line'] =  X_train['num_late_payments'] / X_train['num_credit_lines']
X_test['late_payments_per_line'] =  X_test['num_late_payments'] / X_test['num_credit_lines']

X_train = X_train.drop(columns = ['loan_id'])
X_test = X_test.drop(columns = ['loan_id'])

title: Hack-a-thon
text:
Preprocessing

I wanted to see if there were any skewed values so I could use a Yeo-Johnson transformation on them, which makes the data a normal distribution.
I picked mean for my simpleimputer because I ran my entire process and mean gave me the quickest and best accuracy.
I ran a simple impute just in case for the cat variables and then a onehotencode because there were only regular categorical (no ordinal) variables.



Code
cat = [
    'home_ownership',
    'loan_purpose',
    'state_region'
]
skew = ['year_debt_to_income_no_loan', 'num_late_payments', 'annual_income', 'loan_amount', 'late_payments_per_line']
num = ['debt_to_income', 'num_credit_lines', 'employment_years', 'has_mortgage', 'monthly_obligations',
       'age', 'credit_score', 'loan_term_months']
skew_values = X_train[num].skew().sort_values(ascending=False)


num_transformer = Pipeline([
    ('imputer', KNNImputer(n_neighbors=5)),
    ('scaler', StandardScaler())
])

skew_transformer = Pipeline([
    ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy = 'median')),
    ('yeo_johnson', PowerTransformer(method = 'yeo-johnson'))
])

cat_transformer = Pipeline([
    ('imputer', SimpleImputer(strategy = 'constant', fill_value='missing')),
    ('onehot', OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown = 'ignore'))
])

preprocessor = ColumnTransformer([
    ('num', num_transformer, num),
    ('skew', skew_transformer, skew),
    ('cat', cat_transformer, cat)
])

title: Hack-a-thon
text:
Model Fit

I used a 5-fold cross-validation strategy repeated 3 times which made sure that each class was represented proportionally.
I tried to run logisticregression, knnclassifier, and randomforestclassifier but I ultimately chose randomforest because it was significantly better.
The final model was tuned by optimizing the number of trees, the max depth, and the number of features of each split.

    max_depth=None,  
    max_features=3,

)

rf_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', preprocessor),
    ('rf', final_rf_model)
])
